flags: Driving descriptions are thin: cache supports endpoints, length, residential growth and markers, but not curves, grades, a canopy or travel time. Kept the overview concise and did not invent ferry history from the road name.

Material supplies no strip towns or miles. Retained I’On then Remley Point as separate excursions and placed Lucas Family Cemetery afterward using cached coordinates; exact access/turn sequence is unverified.
Added Lucas Family Cemetery to meet the three-moment minimum. Its focused cache supports a short account, not current public access.

Remley Point's larger burial count is residents' qualified estimate. The cached secondary source supports the 2005 no-development ruling, not a transfer of ownership or a current visitation right; no court record or community-authored source is cached.

Current claims were re-found; none had to be dropped for lack of cache support. I’On's development litigation was omitted for focus, rather than conflated with the separate later HOA amenities lawsuit.
